label: rem:classical-limit-adelic-assembly
title: Adelic-assembly reading of $\mathcal{L}$ and phase-decoherence non-fullness
html:
Adelic-assembly perspective (preferred reading). Equivalently, \mathcal{L} is the archimedean component of the realization tower \{\rho_v\}_{v \in \mathrm{Pl}(\mathbb{Q})} of the motivic substrate. Under this reading, \mathbf{C}_q is the universal motive over \widehat{\mathcal{M}}. Each finite place p of \mathbb{Q} (adelic substrate) carries a local realization \rho_p landing in \mathbb{Q}_p. The archimedean place v = \infty carries \rho_\infty = \mathcal{L}, landing in \mathbb{R}. The q \to 1 limit is the vanishing of the local Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon_\infty at the archimedean place. The classical continuum is what remains after that single local \varepsilon_v is collapsed.

Non-fullness of \mathcal{L}: phase decoherence. The full motivic class [X] \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} carries the relative q-phases between all finite places. The archimedean projection \rho_\infty collapses across all those phases, retaining only the real-valued shadow. That collapse is the loss of quantum information: the classical continuum sees only the archimedean projection of the unglued adelic motives.
